## Coverage and interpretation

The table contains all 11 reported benefit/cost ratios and standard errors from Table 6 of the August 2, 2018 author manuscript. The pooled life-cycle, all-benefits baseline (7.33; standard error 1.84) appears first, followed by the other source cells in manuscript order. These are alternative forecasts using related data, not 11 independent studies. The Kline–Walters-style estimates are García and colleagues' application of that forecasting method, not results directly reported by Kline and Walters. The missing authors'-method cell for Chetty-based age-27 inputs is not reported, not zero. [Source manuscript](https://cehd.uchicago.edu/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/abc_comprehensivecba_revised_2018-08-02a_jlg.pdf).

## Comparison assumptions

The baseline discounts benefits and costs to birth at 3% and forecasts through age 79. The reported ratio averages bootstrap ratios; it is not necessarily the ratio of rounded aggregate means. Control childcare substitution costs enter the authors' benefits accounting. Forecasts combine experimental and nonexperimental data.

## Cost caveat

The 2018 appendix's listed annual cost components do not reconcile to its reported total. Author-reported estimates are preserved; independently reconstructed cost-effectiveness rankings remain unresolved. The two underlying trials and alternate forecast specifications must not be counted as independent replications.
